blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Operating across multiple jurisdictions turns employment law from a compliance exercise into a governance discipline. What is lawful — and sensible — in one country may be unlawful, or simply unwise, in another. Termination procedures that take a week in one jurisdiction can take months or years in another, with significantly different financial and reputational exposures.

The sensible approach is to build a clear global framework — covering non-negotiable principles such as dignity, non-discrimination and due process — and then allow local teams, supported by qualified counsel, to adapt the specifics. Attempts to impose a single set of detailed procedures globally tend to fail, as the local legal nuances are too important to be managed centrally.

Governance considerations have grown alongside legal ones. Regulators, investors and large clients increasingly request evidence of sound employment practices across the full supply chain, not merely in the head office. HR functions that treat global compliance as a cost centre rather than a governance discipline are regularly surprised by the scale of risk they have been quietly accumulating.

items.q: According to the text, operating across multiple jurisdictions turns employment law into…
options: a matter for the head office alone
a fixed set of global procedures
items.why: "turns employment law from a compliance exercise into a governance discipline."

items.q: What does the text recommend for handling the specifics in each country?
options: Letting local teams, supported by qualified counsel, adapt them
Leaving them entirely to head-office lawyers
items.why: "allow local teams, supported by qualified counsel, to adapt the specifics."

items.q: Why do attempts to impose a single set of detailed procedures globally tend to fail?
options: Local legal nuances are too important to be managed centrally
items.why: "the local legal nuances are too important to be managed centrally."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A shared set of principles can hold across borders.
Detailed termination steps should be identical in every country.
Compliance risk can build up without being noticed.
Local counsel adds real value to global HR.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que procedimentos detalhados uniformes fracassam; princípios são globais, procedimentos são locais.

items.q: The phrase "risk they have been quietly accumulating" suggests that…
options: the risk is deliberately hidden by executives
the danger grows unnoticed until it becomes large
the risk is always financial rather than legal
the risk disappears once compliance is centralised
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" indica que o risco cresce em silêncio, sem ser percebido, até assumir grande escala.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentando a revisão de governança à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. Over the past six weeks I've been leading a governance review across our twelve operating countries, and I want to be candid about what we've found before we get into the recommendations.

The headline is this: we do not have a compliance problem in the narrow sense. Our lawyers are good, our contracts are sound. What we have is a governance problem. Each country has been solving its own employment issues in isolation, and nobody has been asking whether the whole thing hangs together. In two markets, termination practices that are perfectly lawful locally would look indefensible if a major client audited our supply chain tomorrow.

So my proposal is deliberately modest on paper. We agree a short set of non-negotiable principles — dignity, due process, non-discrimination — and we hold every country to those. Everything below that line stays local, guided by qualified counsel on the ground. I am not asking you to write a global rulebook; those always collapse under the weight of local nuance.

What I am asking for is a mandate to treat this as governance, not cost. If we keep booking compliance as a line item to be minimised, we will keep accumulating risk we cannot see — and one day a regulator or a client will see it for us.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Charlotte characterise the central finding of her review?
options: The company has a serious compliance problem in the narrow sense
The company has a governance problem, not a narrow compliance one
The company's contracts are legally unsound
The company needs a single global rulebook
items.why: "we do not have a compliance problem in the narrow sense… What we have is a governance problem."

items.q: What does Charlotte say has been happening across the twelve countries?
options: Each country has been solving its issues in isolation
Every country has adopted the same procedures
Head office has approved every local decision
The countries have stopped hiring lawyers
items.why: "Each country has been solving its own employment issues in isolation."

items.q: What does Charlotte actually ask the leadership for?
options: A budget increase for local lawyers
A mandate to treat the issue as governance, not cost
Permission to write a detailed global rulebook
Approval to close two operating countries
items.why: "What I am asking for is a mandate to treat this as governance, not cost."

items.q: When Charlotte says her proposal is "deliberately modest on paper," she implies that…
options: the proposal is unimportant and can be ignored
its simplicity is intentional, though its impact is significant
she has not finished writing it
the board asked her to keep it short
items.why: Inferência: "deliberately" mostra que a simplicidade é uma escolha estratégica — poucos princípios firmes, não falta de substância.

items.q: What does Charlotte warn will happen if compliance keeps being booked as a cost to minimise?
options: The company will keep accumulating unseen risk until an outsider exposes it
Head office will lose control of contracts
Clients will refuse to sign new deals
items.why: Inferência: "we will keep accumulating risk we cannot see — and one day a regulator or a client will see it for us."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A dismissal that is routine in one jurisdiction can be litigated for years in another." A jurisdiction is…
options: a country or territory with its own body of law
items.why: Jurisdiction = jurisdição: o território sob determinado ordenamento jurídico.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Before terminating anyone, we must show that ___ was followed — notice, a hearing and a documented reason."
items.why: Due process = devido processo: o procedimento justo (aviso, oitiva, motivo documentado).

items.q: "The board asked for external counsel before signing off on the redundancy plan." Counsel here means…
items.why: Counsel = assessoria jurídica; nesse contexto, os advogados qualificados que orientam a decisão.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A leaked dismissal video created serious ___ — the story ran in the press for a week."
items.why: Reputational exposure = exposição reputacional: o risco à imagem que se materializou na imprensa.

items.q: "Auditors now trace labour practices across the entire supply chain." The supply chain refers to…
options: the full network of suppliers and partners that feed the business
items.why: Supply chain = cadeia de suprimentos: toda a rede de fornecedores e parceiros, não só a matriz.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de governança e compliance. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal will have to sign off on the new termination protocol before rollout." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the governance framework country by country over two quarters." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, aqui país a país.

items.q: "Two country managers pushed back on the centralised approach." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar por completo.

items.q: "HR agreed the principles but never followed through on the local training." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Ignoring accumulating risk today only stores up trouble for later." To store up trouble means to…
options: create future problems that will surface later
items.why: Store up trouble = acumular problemas que vão estourar mais adiante — eco do 'risk accumulation' da lição.
